messages:
maya: Heads up — we've observed three tenant pools in us-west2 with recurring tail latency spikes that look network-driven. p95 is stable but p99 for inference RPCs jumps ~700-900ms during short egress bursts.

sam: Do we have packet counters / NIC queue stats to tie it to egress? sounds like noisy neighbor egress saturation. :thinking:

maya: Yep — checked tx_queue_stats and ifcfg counters. See snippet from last spike window: drops rising 0 -> 1.2k in ~30s, txq_full events + kernel offload fallbacks.

leo: I pulled the node logs earlier. NIC interrupts spike, and we see lots of small flows from a single tenant IP range. That tenant has a heavy concurrent streaming workload (many short-lived connections).

irene: Could be KV-cache misses causing lots of small responses. But the symptom is clearly egress shaping needed.

sam: Short-term mitigation options? node-level tc policing per-tenant? SmartNIC rate limit? Dedicated pools for the offending tenant?

leo: Quick test using tc on a dev node helped smooth the tail. Example I used (manual trial):
```
# limit tenant traffic to 500mbit
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 30
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 10gbit
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1:1 classid 1:10 htb rate 500mbit ceil 10gbit
# mark packets in iptables for tenant subnet 10.40.5.0/24
iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -d 10.40.5.0/24 -j MARK --set-mark 10
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 handle 10 fw flowid 1:10
```
It reduced the p99 on that node from ~850ms to ~220ms for a short window. But this is brittle at scale and needs proper per-pod marking integration with CNI.

maya: Good proof. Long-term we shouldn't rely on ad-hoc tc per node. Proposal: implement per-tenant egress fairness in two phases — Phase A: host-level eBPF police that maps tenant IDs from pod metadata and enforces token-bucket shaping (low risk, incremental rollout). Phase B: CNI/SmartNIC offload for high-throughput tenants to avoid CPU hit.

irene: How invasive is Phase A? Will it affect latency for small requests? We need to keep short RPCs snappy.

leo: eBPF token bucket at socket/NIC egress can be tuned with burst allowance to preserve tail for small RPCs while smoothing long bursts. CPU overhead is measurable but acceptable on our inference nodes if we pin the agent to a mgmt core.

sam: Alternatives: move offending tenants to dedicated pools. That buys isolation but increases cost. Rough estimate: dedicated pool reserve adds ~20% GPU capacity per tenant peak to maintain headroom. Also scheduling churn for migration.

maya: Cost / ops tradeoffs noted. For now suggest we implement Phase A on a handful of trial nodes in us-west2 and add per-tenant egress metrics + alerting. If specific tenants still cause issues, escalate to dedicated pools.

devops-oncall: I can deploy the eBPF probe to a canary AZ tonight if we have the build. What metrics do we want ingested?

maya: Thanks. Send metrics for: per-tenant egress rate, per-tenant burst_count, node-level tx_drops, p99_inference_latency_by_tenant. Also a boolean flag when shaping is active.

infra-bot: New experiment created: egress-fairness-phaseA-canary. Targets: us-west2-a nodes 5-8. Alert: p99_inference_latency_by_tenant > 500ms for 3m.

sam: Rollout plan idea: enable shaping in monitor-only mode first (collect metrics but don't drop), run for 24h to get baselines, then enable enforcement with conservative bursts.

leo: I'll draft a CNI hook for iptables/netfilter marking so we can map pod -> tenant mark reliably. Will also prototype a BPF program and share perf numbers.

irene: Who owns migration to dedicated pools if we need it? Product needs to coordinate with customer before forced migration.

maya: Product will own customer comms. Infra will own the migration tooling (live drain + rebind). For the immediate action items:
- leo: prototype CNI marking + eBPF (ETA 48h)
- devops-oncall: deploy canary experiment tonight and wire metrics (ETA 6h)
- sam: cost model for dedicated pool isolation (ETA 72h)

sam: One more ask — add a tag to logs marking if traffic was being shaped so we can correlate with SLO regressions.

maya: Good call. Let's reconvene after we have 24h of monitor-only data. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
